summary: Simon Winant works in Indology and linguistics. He studied as a PhD student at Ghent University and was attested as a faculty member there in 2026.

Simon Wong is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of British Columbia in Dermatology and Skin Science, and at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, where he was attested as professor in 2010.
Singhathon Narāsabho worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University, studying under doctoral supervisor Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Siniruddha Dash specializes in Indology and linguistics. He served as director at the University of Madras (2000–2014), the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 2013), and the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation (2020).

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1960–1966), the University of London (~1966–1968), and Harvard (~1980–1988), under Frank Raymond Allchin. He served as Director General of Archaeology in Sri Lanka (~1992–2001).

Sisir Roy is a scholar in philosophy who studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He held a professorship at the Indian Statistical Institute in 1993 and a post at the National Institute of Advanced Studies, attested in 2009.
Sita Krishna Nambiar was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn under doctoral supervisor Paul Hacker. She held an academic post at Indraprastha College for Women.

Sita Ram Roy was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Anant Sadashiv Altekar and Ram Sharan Sharma (1962). He held posts at K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, Bihar's Directorate of Archaeology and Museums (1971), and Gaya Museum (1971).

Siu-tong Kwan specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and also studied under Zhihua Yao until 2005.
Sivadatta Sarma was an Indologist who served as a Sanskrit teacher and professor at Maharaja Sanskrit College, Jaipur, with posts attested in 1892 and 1929.
Siyong Liang was an archaeologist and historian. He pursued his education at Tsinghua University and Harvard University (~1924–1930).
Smita Halder is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Susmita Basu Majumdar. In 2026, she was attested as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

So Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who received an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and Meijo University (associate professor attested 1977–1978; professor attested 1991).

Sodo Mori, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Komazawa and Tokyo universities under Kogen Mizuno, Hajime Nakamura, and G. P. Malalasekera. He held professorships at Josai University (1977) and Aichi Gakuin University (1991–2003).
Sodo Yokoyama was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Ekō Hashimoto (~1930) and Kodo Sawaki at Antai-ji (1949–1957). He taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Nakagawa was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), and under Gempo Yamamoto (~1931–1961). His students included Robert Baker Aitken, Philip Kapleau, and Maurine Stuart.

Sofija Aleksandrovna Černikova was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the National University of Uzbekistan (~1953–1958) and the University of Delhi (1963–1964). She taught at the National University of Uzbekistan, becoming docent in 1970.

Sogaku Harada was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University, training under Dokutan Sōsan and others. He was a professor at Komazawa University (1911–1923) and taught Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani and Philip Kapleau.
Sogen Asahina was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Nihon University. He held a post at Kanagawa University and taught Koun Yamada and Kyozo Yamada.

Sogen Omori was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Nihon University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot at Koho-in (1947), founded Chozen-ji (1972), and was professor (1970) and president (1978–1982) at Hanazono University.
